options.name: -k
options.description: Only run tests which match the given substring expression. An expression is a python evaluatable expression where all names are substring-matched against test names and their parent classes. Example: -k 'test_method or test_other' matches all test functions and classes whose name contains 'test_method' or 'test_other', while -k 'not test_method' matches those that don't contain 'test_method' in their names. -k 'not test_method and not test_other' will eliminate the matches. Additionally keywords are matched to classes and functions containing extra names in their 'extra_keyword_matches' set, as well as functions which have names assigned directly to them. The matching is case- insensitive

options.description: Version for Qodana

subcommands.name: init
subcommands.description: Configure project for Qodana

options.name: -i
options.description: Root directory of the project to configure (default ".")

subcommands.name: scan
subcommands.description: Scan a project with Qodana

options.name: -a
options.description: Unique report identifier (GUID) to be used by Qodana Cloud

options.name: -b
options.description: Provide the path to an existing SARIF report to be used in the baseline state calculation

options.name: --baseline-include-absent
options.description: Include in the output report the results from the baseline run that are absent in the current run

options.name: --cache-dir
options.description: Override cache directory (default <userCacheDir>/JetBrains/<linter>/cache)

options.name: -c
options.description: Override the docker image to be used for the analysis

options.name: --clear-cache
options.description: Clear the local Qodana cache before running the analysis

options.name: --disable-sanity
options.description: Skip running the inspections configured by the sanity profile

options.name: -e
options.description: Define additional environment variables for the Qodana container (you can use the flag multiple times). CLI is not reading full host environment variables and does not pass it to the Qodana container for security reasons

options.name: --fail-threshold
options.description: Set the number of problems that will serve as a quality gate. If this number is reached, the inspection run is terminated with a non-zero exit code

options.name: -l
options.description: Override linter to use

options.name: --port
options.description: Port to serve the report on (default 8080)

options.name: --print-problems
options.description: Print all found problems by Qodana in the CLI output

options.name: -n
options.description: Profile name defined in the project

options.name: -p
options.description: Path to the profile file

options.name: -i
options.description: Root directory of the inspected project (default ".")

options.name: --property
options.description: Set a JVM property to be used while running Qodana using the --property property.name=value1,value2,...,valueN notation

options.name: -o
options.description: Override directory to save Qodana inspection results to (default <userCacheDir>/JetBrains/<linter>/results)

options.name: --run-promo
options.description: Set to 'true' to have the application run the inspections configured by the promo profile; set to 'false' otherwise (default: 'true' only if Qodana is executed with the default profile)

options.name: -s
options.description: Generate HTML report (default true)

options.name: --script
options.description: Override the run scenario (default "default")

options.name: --send-report
options.description: Send the inspection report to Qodana Cloud, requires the '--token' option to be specified

options.name: -w
options.description: Serve HTML report on port

options.name: --skip-pull
options.description: Skip pulling the latest Qodana container

options.name: -d
options.description: Directory inside the project-dir directory must be inspected. If not specified, the whole project is inspected

options.name: --stub-profile
options.description: Absolute path to the fallback profile file. This option is applied in case the profile was not specified using any available options

options.name: -u
options.description: User to run Qodana container as. Please specify user id – '$UID' or user id and group id $(id -u):$(id -g). Use 'root' to run as the root user (default: the current user)

options.name: -v
options.description: Define additional volumes for the Qodana container (you can use the flag multiple times)

options.name: -r

options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. options.name: -T
options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. Each "--to-except" parameter expands this selection to include all dependencies of PROJECT, but not PROJECT itself. "." can be used as shorthand for the project in the current working directory. For details, refer to the website article "Selecting subsets of projects"

script: until [[ -f rush.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat rush.json

options.name: -f
options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. Each "--from" parameter expands this selection to include PROJECT and all projects that depend on it, plus all dependencies of this set.  "." can be used as shorthand for the project in the current working directory. For details, refer to the website article "Selecting subsets of projects"

script: until [[ -f rush.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat rush.json

options.name: -o
options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. Each "--only" parameter expands this selection to include PROJECT; its dependencies are not added. "." can be used as shorthand for the project in the current working directory. Note that this parameter is "unsafe" as it may produce a selection that excludes some dependencies. For details, refer to the website article "Selecting subsets of projects"

script: until [[ -f rush.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat rush.json

options.name: -i
options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. Each "--impacted-by" parameter expands this selection to include PROJECT and any projects that depend on PROJECT (and thus might be broken by changes to PROJECT). "." can be used as shorthand for the project in the current working directory. Note that this parameter is "unsafe" as it may produce a selection that excludes some dependencies. For details, refer to the website article "Selecting subsets of projects"

script: until [[ -f rush.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat rush.json

options.name: -I
options.description: Normally all projects in the monorepo will be processed; adding this parameter will instead select a subset of projects. Each "--impacted-by-except" parameter works the same as "--impacted-by" except that PROJECT itself is not added to the selection. "." can be used as shorthand for the project in the current working directory. Note that this parameter is "unsafe" as it may produce a selection that excludes some dependencies. For details, refer to the website article "Selecting subsets of projects"

script: until [[ -f rush.json ]] || [[ $PWD = '/' ]]; do cd ..; done; cat rush.json

commands.name: scp
commands.description: Copies files or directories between hosts on a network

options.description:
Copies between two remote hosts are transferred through the local
host.  Without this option the data is copied directly between the
two remote hosts.  Note that this option disables the progress
meter and selects batch mode for the second host, since scp cannot
ask for passwords or passphrases for both hosts
Forces scp to use IPv4 addresses only
Forces scp to use IPv6 addresses only

options.name: -A
options.description: Allows forwarding of ssh-agent(1) to the remote system. The default is not to forward an authentication agent

options.name: -B
options.description: Selects batch mode (prevents asking for passwords or passphrases)

options.name: -C
options.description: Compression enable. Passes the -C flag to ssh(1) to enable compression

options.name: -c
options.description: Selects the cipher to use for encrypting the data transfer. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -F
options.description: Specifies an alternative per-user configuration file for ssh. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -i
options.description: Selects the file from which the identity (private key) for public key authentication is read. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -J
options.description:
Connect to the target host by first making an scp connection to the
jump host described by destination and then establishing a TCP
forwarding to the ultimate destination from there.  Multiple jump
hops may be specified separated by comma characters.  This is a
shortcut to specify a ProxyJump configuration directive.  This
option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -l
options.description: Limits the used bandwidth, specified in Kbit/s

options.name: -o
options.description:
Can be used to pass options to ssh in the format used in
ssh_config(5).  This is useful for specifying options for which
there is no separate scp command-line flag.  For full details of
the options listed below, and their possible values, see
ssh_config(5)

options.name: -P
options.description:
Specifies the port to connect to on the remote host.  Note that
this option is written with a capital ‘P’, because -p is already
reserved for preserving the times and modes of the file

options.name: -p
options.description: Preserves modification times, access times, and modes from the original file

options.name: -q
options.description: Quiet mode: disables the progress meter as well as warning and diagnostic messages from ssh(1)

options.name: -r
options.description: Recursively copy entire directories.  Note that scp follows symbolic links encountered in the tree traversal

options.name: -S
options.description: Name of program to use for the encrypted connection.  The program must understand ssh(1) options

options.name: -T
options.description:
Disable strict filename checking.  By default when copying files
from a remote host to a local directory scp checks that the
received filenames match those requested on the command-line to
prevent the remote end from sending unexpected or unwanted files.
Because of differences in how various operating systems and shells
interpret filename wildcards, these checks may cause wanted files
to be rejected.  This option disables these checks at the expense
of fully trusting that the server will not send unexpected
filenames

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose mode.  Causes scp and ssh(1) to print debugging messages about their progress. This is helpful in debugging connection, authentication, and configuration problems

commands.name: sed
commands.description: Stream editor

options.name: -E
options.description: Interprets regular expressions as extended (modern) regular expressions rather than basic regular expressions

options.name: -a
options.description: Causes sed to delay opening each file until a command containing the related ``w'' function is applied to a line of input

options.name: -e
options.description: Appends the editing commands specified by the command argument to the list of commands

options.name: -f
options.description: Appends the editing commands found in the file command_file to the list of commands. The editing commands should each be listed on a separate line

options.name: -I
options.description: Edits files in-place, saving backups with the specified extension.  If a zero-length extension is given, no backup will be saved

options.name: -i
options.description: Edits files in-place similarly to `-I`, but treats each file independently from other files.  In particular, line numbers in each file start at 1, the ``$'' address matches the last line of the current file, and address ranges are limited to the current file

options.name: -l
options.description: Makes output line buffered

options.name: -n
options.description: By default, each line of input is echoed to the standard output after all of the commands have been applied to it.  The `-n` option suppresses this behavior

options.name: -r
options.description: Same as `-E` for compatibility with GNU sed

options.name: -u
options.description: Makes output unbuffered

subcommands.name: a
subcommands.description: Appends `text` after a line

subcommands.name: b
subcommands.description: Branch unconditionally to `label`

subcommands.name: c
subcommands.description: Replace (change) lines with `text`

subcommands.name: d
subcommands.description: Delete the pattern space; immediately start next cycle

subcommands.name: D
subcommands.description: If pattern space contains newlines, delete text in the pattern space up to the first newline, and restart cycle with the resultant pattern space, without reading a new line of input. If pattern space contains no newline, start a normal new cycle as if the d command was issued

subcommands.name: e
subcommands.description: Executes the command that is found in pattern space and replaces the pattern space with the output; a trailing newline is suppressed

subcommands.name: F
subcommands.description: Prints the file name of the current input file

subcommands.name: g
subcommands.description: Replaces the contents of the pattern space with the contents of the hold space

subcommands.name: G
subcommands.description: Appends a newline to the contents of the pattern space, and then appends the contents of the hold space to that of the pattern space

subcommands.name: h
subcommands.description: Replaces the contents of the hold space with the contents of the pattern space

subcommands.name: H
subcommands.description: Appends a newline to the contents of the hold space, and then appends the contents of the pattern space to that of the hold space

subcommands.name: i
subcommands.description: Insert text before a line

subcommands.name: l
subcommands.description: Prints the pattern space in an unambiguous form

subcommands.name: n
subcommands.description: Prints the pattern space, then, regardless, replaces the pattern space with the next line of input. If there is no more input then sed exits without processing any more commands

subcommands.name: N
subcommands.description: Adds a newline to the pattern space, then appends the next line of input to the pattern space. If there is no more input then sed exits without processing any more commands

subcommands.name: p
subcommands.description: Prints the pattern space

subcommands.name: P
subcommands.description: Prints the pattern space up to the first newline

subcommands.name: q
subcommands.description: Exit sed without processing any more commands or input

subcommands.name: Q
subcommands.description: This command is the same as q, but will not print the contents of pattern space

subcommands.name: r
subcommands.description: Reads file

subcommands.name: R
subcommands.description: Queue a line of filename to be read and inserted into the output stream at the end of the current cycle, or when the next input line is read

subcommands.name: s
subcommands.description: Match the regular-expression against the content of the pattern space. If found, replace matched string with replacement

subcommands.name: t
subcommands.description: (test) Branch to label only if there has been a successful substitution since the last input line was read or conditional branch was taken. The label may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started

subcommands.name: T
subcommands.description: (test) Branch to label only if there have been no successful substitutions since the last input line was read or conditional branch was taken. The label may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started

subcommands.name: v
subcommands.description: Makes sed fail if GNU sed extensions are not supported, or if the requested version is not available

subcommands.name: w
subcommands.description: Writes the pattern space to the file

subcommands.name: W
subcommands.description: Writes to the given filename the portion of the pattern space up to the first newline

subcommands.name: x
subcommands.description: Exchanges the contents of the hold and pattern spaces

subcommands.name: y
subcommands.description: Transliterate any characters in the pattern space which match any of the source-chars with the corresponding character in dest-chars

subcommands.name: z
subcommands.description: (zap) Empties the content of pattern space
Comment until the next newline

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help for sftp
Forces scp to use IPv4 addresses only
Forces scp to use IPv6 addresses only

options.name: -A
options.description: Allows forwarding of ssh-agent(1) to the remote system. The default is not to forward an authentication agent

options.name: -a
options.description:
Attempt to continue interrupted transfers rather than overwriting
existing partial or complete copies of files.  If the partial
contents differ from those being transferred, then the resultant
file is likely to be corrupt

options.name: -B
options.description:
Specify the size of the buffer that sftp uses when transferring
files.  Larger buffers require fewer round trips at the cost of
higher memory consumption.  The default is 32768 bytes

options.name: -b
options.description:
Batch mode reads a series of commands from an input batchfile
instead of stdin.  Since it lacks user interaction it should be
used in conjunction with non-interactive authentication to obviate
the need to enter a password at connection time (see sshd(8) and
ssh-keygen(1) for details)

options.name: -C
options.description: Compression enable. Passes the -C flag to ssh(1) to enable compression

options.name: -c
options.description: Selects the cipher to use for encrypting the data transfer. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -D
options.description:
Connect directly to a local sftp server (rather than via ssh(1)).
This option may be useful in debugging the client and server

options.name: -F
options.description: Specifies an alternative per-user configuration file for ssh. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -f
options.description: Requests that files be flushed to disk immediately after transfer

options.name: -i
options.description: Selects the file from which the identity (private key) for public key authentication is read. This option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -J
options.description:
Connect to the target host by first making an scp connection to the
jump host described by destination and then establishing a TCP
forwarding to the ultimate destination from there.  Multiple jump
hops may be specified separated by comma characters.  This is a
shortcut to specify a ProxyJump configuration directive.  This
option is directly passed to ssh(1)

options.name: -l
options.description: Limits the used bandwidth, specified in Kbit/s

options.name: -N
options.description: Disables quiet mode, e.g. to override the implicit quiet mode set by the -b flag

options.name: -o
options.description:
Can be used to pass options to ssh in the format used in
ssh_config(5).  This is useful for specifying options for which
there is no separate scp command-line flag.  For full details of
the options listed below, and their possible values, see
ssh_config(5)

options.name: -P
options.description:
Specifies the port to connect to on the remote host.  Note that
this option is written with a capital ‘P’, because -p is already
reserved for preserving the times and modes of the file

options.name: -p
options.description: Preserves modification times, access times, and modes from the original file

options.name: -q
options.description: Quiet mode: disables the progress meter as well as warning and diagnostic messages from ssh(1)

options.name: -R
options.description:
Specify how many requests may be outstanding at any one time.
Increasing this may slightly improve file transfer speed but will
increase memory usage.  The default is 64 outstanding requests

options.name: -r
options.description: Recursively copy entire directories.  Note that scp follows symbolic links encountered in the tree traversal

options.name: -S
options.description: Name of program to use for the encrypted connection.  The program must understand ssh(1) options

options.name: -s
options.description:
Specifies the SSH2 subsystem or the path for an sftp server on the
remote host.  A path is useful when the remote sshd(8) does not
have an sftp subsystem configured

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose mode.  Causes scp and ssh(1) to print debugging messages about their progress. This is helpful in debugging connection, authentication, and configuration problems

Set the location to a series of waypoints specified as 'lat,lon' pairs, interpolating between them over time.
At least two waypoints are required. Use '-' to read waypoints from stdin, one waypoint per li
Speed specifies how quickly to move between waypoints in meters per second. If not specified 20m/s is us
The system will issue location updates along the path between each pair of waypoints. Use distance or interval to 
control how often those updates are issued. Distance will issue an update every <meters> travelled without regard
for the time between updates. Interval will issue updates at fixed times without regard for how much
the location moves between updates.
If neither are specified an interval of 1.0 seconds is used. If both are specified the system picks on
Example simulating a direct line between San Francisco and New York City, with updates every km:
set --distance=1000 --speed=260 37.629538,-122.395733 40.628083,-73.768254

subcommands.name: match set
subcommands.description:
Override the SDK to runtime build mapping. This controls which build of a given runtime Xcode will prefer for building and running when using that SDK. This matters most often during Beta releases when there are multiple builds for a given OS version. If --sdkBuild is not specified it is assumed you mean the SDK build for the currently selected Xcode.

Note: Remember this is about build numbers, not semantic versions. When using the iOS 16.0 SDK Xcwill always prefer an iOS 16.0 runtime. Matching policy controls what to do when there are multiiOS 16.0 runtimes availabeg if the iOS 16.0 SDK is 20A245 and the available runtimes are (20A248, 20A252, 20A254) which should Xcode use for building, SwiftUI Previews, and when launching iOS 16.0 Simulators? They are all iOS 16.0 runtimes so a policy must decide which one is selected

options.description: Use size for the maximum size of the memory buffer

options.description: Store temporary files in the directory dir

options.name: -u
options.description: Unique keys. Suppress all lines that have a key that is equal to an already processed one

options.name: -s
options.description: Stable sort. This option maintains the original record order of records that have an equal key

options.description: Ignore leading blank characters when comparing lines

options.description: Consider only blank spaces and alphanumeric characters in comparisons

options.description: Convert all lowercase characters to their upper case equivalent before comparison

options.name: -g
options.description: Sort by general numerical value

options.description: Sort by numerical value, but take into account the SI suffix, if present

options.description: Ignore all non-printable characters

options.name: -M
options.description: Sort by month abbreviations.  Unknown strings are considered smaller than the month names

options.name: -n
options.description: Sort fields numerically by arithmetic value

options.name: -R
options.description: Sort by a random order

options.name: -r
options.description: Sort in reverse order

options.name: -V
options.description: Sort version numbers

options.name: -k
options.description: Define a restricted sort key that has the starting position field1, and optional ending position field2

options.name: -t
options.description: Use char as a field separator character

options.name: -z
options.description: Use NUL as record separator

options.name: --batch-size
options.description: Specify maximum number of files that can be opened by sort at once

options.name: --compress-program
options.description: Use PROGRAM to compress temporary files (eg. bzip2)

options.name: --random-source
options.description: In random sort, the file content is used as the source of the 'seed' data for the hash function choice

options.name: --debug
options.description: Print some extra information about the sorting process to the standard output

options.name: --parallel
options.description: Set the maximum number of execution threads.  Default number equals to the number of CPUs

options.name: --files0-from
options.description: Take the input file list from the file filename

options.name: --radixsort
options.description: Try to use radix sort, if the sort specifications allow

options.name: --mmap
options.description: Try to use file memory mapping system call.  It may increase speed in some cases

options.description: Select how to sort values

options.name: -r

options.name: -t

options.description: Send verbose output to standard error describing what Stow is doing. Verbosity levels are from 0 to 5; 0 is the default. Using '-v' or '--verbose' increases the verbosity by one; using `--verbose=N' sets it to N

options.name: -S
options.description: Stow the packages that follow this option into the target directory. This is the default action and so can be omitted if you are only stowing packages rather than performing a mixture of stow/delete/restow actions

options.description: Unstow the packages that follow this option from the target directory rather than installing them

options.description: Restow packages (first unstow, then stow again). This is useful for pruning obsolete symlinks from the target tree after updating the software in a package

options.name: --adopt
options.description: This behaviour is specifically intended to alter the contents of your stow directory.  If you do not want that, this option is not for you

options.description: Disable folding of newly stowed directories when stowing, and refolding of newly foldable directories when unstowing

options.description: Ignore files ending in this Perl regex

options.name: --defer
options.description: Don't stow files beginning with this Perl regex if the file is already stowed to another package

options.name: --override
options.description: Force stowing files beginning with this Perl regex if the file is already stowed to another package

options.name: --dotfiles
options.description: Enable special handling for 'dotfiles' (files or folders whose name begins with a period) in the package directory. If this option is enabled, Stow will add a preprocessing step for each file or folder whose name begins with 'dot - ', and replace the 'dot- ' prefix in the name by a period (.). This is useful when Stow is used to manage collections of dotfiles, to avoid having a package directory full of hidden files

options.name: --terragrunt-config
options.description: Path to the Terragrunt config file. Default is terragrunt.hcl

options.name: --terragrunt-tfpath
options.description: Path to the Terraform binary. Default is terraform (on PATH)

options.name: --terragrunt-no-auto-init
options.description: Don't automatically run 'terraform init' during other terragrunt commands. You must run 'terragrunt init' manually

options.name: --terragrunt-no-auto-retry
options.description: Don't automatically re-run command in case of transient errors

options.name: --terragrunt-non-interactive
options.description: Assume 'yes' for all prompts

options.name: --terragrunt-working-dir
options.description: The path to the Terraform templates. Default is current directory

options.name: --terragrunt-download-dir
options.description: The path where to download Terraform code. Default is .terragrunt-cache in the working directory

options.name: --terragrunt-source
options.description: Download Terraform configurations from the specified source into a temporary folder, and run Terraform in that temporary folder

options.name: --terragrunt-source-map
options.description: Replaces any source URL (including the source URL of a config pulled in with dependency blocks) that has root source with dest

options.name: --terragrunt-source-update
options.description: Delete the contents of the temporary folder to clear out any old, cached source code before downloading new source code into it

options.name: --terragrunt-ignore-dependency-errors
options.description: *-all commands continue processing components even if a dependency fails

options.name: --terragrunt-iam-role
options.description: Assume the specified IAM role before executing Terraform. Can also be set via the TERRAGRUNT_IAM_ROLE environment variable

options.name: --terragrunt-iam-assume-role-duration
options.description: Session duration for IAM Assume Role session. Can also be set via the TERRAGRUNT_IAM_ASSUME_ROLE_DURATION environment variable

options.name: --terragrunt-iam-assume-role-session-name
options.description: Name for the IAM Assummed Role session. Can also be set via TERRAGRUNT_IAM_ASSUME_ROLE_SESSION_NAME environment variable

options.name: --terragrunt-exclude-dir
options.description: Unix-style glob of directories to exclude when running *-all commands

options.name: --terragrunt-include-dir
options.description: Unix-style glob of directories to include when running *-all commands

options.name: --terragrunt-strict-include
options.description: Only modules under the directories passed in with –terragrunt-include-dir will be included. All dependencies of the included directories will be excluded if they are not in the included directories. If no –terragrunt-include-dir flags are included, terragrunt will not include any modules during the execution of the commands

options.name: --terragrunt-strict-validate
options.description: Sets strict mode for the validate-inputs command. By default, strict mode is off. When this flag is passed, strict mode is turned on. When strict mode is turned off, the validate-inputs command will only return an error if required inputs are missing from all input sources (env vars, var files, etc). When strict mode is turned on, an error will be returned if required inputs are missing OR if unused variables are passed to Terragrunt

options.name: --terragrunt-ignore-dependency-order
options.description: *-all commands will be run disregarding the dependencies

options.name: --terragrunt-ignore-external-dependencies
options.description: *-all commands will not attempt to include external dependencies

options.name: --terragrunt-include-external-dependencies
options.description: *-all commands will include external dependencies

options.name: --terragrunt-parallelism
options.description: *-all commands parallelism set to at most N modules

options.name: --terragrunt-debug
options.description: Write terragrunt-debug.tfvars to working folder to help root-cause issues

options.name: --terragrunt-log-level
options.description: Sets the logging level for Terragrunt. Supported levels: panic, fatal, error, warn (default), info, debug, trace

options.name: --terragrunt-check
options.description: Enable check mode in the hclfmt command

options.name: --terragrunt-hclfmt-file
options.description: The path to a single hcl file that the hclfmt command should run on

options.name: --terragrunt-override-attr
options.description: A key=value attribute to override in a provider block as part of the aws-provider-patch command. May be specified multiple times

options.name: --terragrunt-json-out
options.description: The file path that terragrunt should use when rendering the terragrunt.hcl config as json. Only used in the render-json command. Defaults to terragrunt_rendered.json

options.name: --terragrunt-modules-that-include
options.description: When passed in, run-all will only run the command against Terragrunt modules that include the specified file

commands.name: traceroute
commands.description: Print the route packets take to network host

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help for traceroute

options.name: -a
options.description: Turn on AS# lookups for each hop encountered

options.name: -A
options.description: Turn on AS# lookups and use the given server instead of the default

options.name: -d
options.description: Enable socket level debugging

options.name: -D
options.description: When an ICMP response to our probe datagram is received, print the differences between the transmitted packet and the packet quoted by the ICMP response. A key showing the location of fields within the transmitted packet is printed, followed by the original packet in hex, followed by the quoted packet in hex. Bytes that are unchanged in the quoted packet are shown as underscores. Note, the IP checksum and the TTL of the quoted packet are not expected to match. By default, only one probe per hop is sent with this option

options.name: -e
options.description: Firewall evasion mode. Use fixed destination ports for UDP and TCP probes. The destination port does NOT increment with each packet sent

options.name: -f
options.description: Set the initial time-to-live used in the first outgoing probe packet

options.name: -F
options.description: Set the `don't fragment` bit

options.name: -g
options.description: Specify a loose source route gateway (8 maximum)

options.name: -i
options.description: Specify a network interface to obtain the source IP address for outgoing probe packets. This is normally only useful on a multihomed host. (See the -s flag for another way to do this.)

options.name: -I
options.description: Use ICMP ECHO instead of UDP datagrams. (A synonym for `-P icmp`)

options.name: -M
options.description: Set the initial time-to-live value used in outgoing probe packets. The default is 1, i.e., start with the first hop

options.name: -m
options.description: Set the max time-to-live (max number of hops) used in outgoing probe packets. The default is net.inet.ip.ttl hops (the same default used for TCP connections)

options.name: -n
options.description: Print hop addresses numerically rather than symbolically and numerically (saves a nameserver address-to-name lookup for each gateway found on the path)

options.name: -P
options.description: Send packets of specified IP protocol. The currently supported protocols are: UDP, TCP, GRE and ICMP Other protocols may also be specified (either by name or by number), though traceroute does not implement any special knowledge of their packet formats. This option is useful for determining which router along a path may be blocking packets based on IP protocol number. But see BUGS below

options.name: -p
options.description: Protocol specific. For UDP and TCP, sets the base port number used in probes (default is 33434). traceroute hopes that nothing is listening on UDP ports base to base+nhops-1 at the destination host (so an ICMP PORT_UNREACHABLE message will be returned to terminate the route tracing). If something is listening on a port in the default range, this option can be used to pick an unused port range

options.name: -q
options.description: Set the number of probes per ``ttl'' to nqueries (default is three probes)

options.name: -r
options.description: Bypass the normal routing tables and send directly to a host on an attached network. If the host is not on a directly-attached network, an error is returned. This option can be used to ping a local host through an interface that has no route through it (e.g., after the interface was dropped by routed(8))

options.name: -s
options.description: Use the following IP address (which must be given as an IP number, not a hostname) as the source address in outgoing probe packets. On hosts with more than one IP address, this option can be used to force the source address to be something other than the IP address of the interface the probe packet is sent on. If the IP address is not one of this machine's interface addresses, an error is returned and nothing is sent. (See the -i flag for another way to do this.)

options.name: -S
options.description: Print a summary of how many probes were not answered for each hop

options.name: -t
options.description: Set the type-of-service in probe packets to the following value (default zero). The value must be a decimal integer in the range 0 to 255. This option can be used to see if different types-of- service result in different paths. (If you are not running a 4.4BSD or later system, this may be academic since the normal network services like telnet and ftp don't let you control the TOS). Not all values of TOS are legal or meaningful - see the IP spec for definitions. Useful values are probably `-t 16' (low delay) and `-t 8' (high throughput)

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose output. Received ICMP packets other than TIME_EXCEEDED and UNREACHABLEs are listed

options.name: -w
options.description: Set the time (in seconds) to wait for a response to a probe (default 5 sec.)

options.name: -x
options.description: Toggle IP checksums. Normally, this prevents traceroute from calculating IP checksums. In some cases, the operating system can overwrite parts of the outgoing packet but not recalculate the checksum (so in some cases the default is to not calculate checksums and using -x causes them to be calculated). Note that checksums are usually required for the last hop when using ICMP ECHO probes ( -I ). So they are always calculated when using ICMP

options.name: -z
options.description: Set the time (in milliseconds) to pause between probes (default 0). Some systems such as Solaris and routers such as Ciscos rate limit ICMP messages. A good value to use with this this is 500 (e.g. 1/2 second)

args.name: file

args.name: artifact_type

subcommands.description: Interactively debug any transaction on the blockchain

options.description: Allows the debugger to compile Solidity test contracts. Implies --compile-all

options.name: --compile-all
options.description: Forces the debugger to recompile all contracts, even when it would otherwise judge doing so unnecessary. Compilation results are not saved

options.name: --compile-none
options.description: Forces the debugger not to recompile contracts, even when it would otherwise judge it necessary. This option is dangerous and may cause errors. Please only use this if you are sure a recompilation is not necessary

args.name: transaction_hash
args.description: Transaction ID to use for debugging. You can omit this to simply start the debugger and then load a transaction later

subcommands.description: Editing your projects is easy; position yourself in a directory where there's a project defined and run the edit command. options.name: --distance
options.description: The search radius, in miles, for a `near_` query.  Can be up to `500` and the default is `25`. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --emergency-address-sid
options.description: The SID of the emergency address configuration to use for emergency calling from the new phone number

options.name: --emergency-status
options.description: The parameter displays if emergency calling is enabled for this number. Active numbers may place emergency calls by dialing valid emergency numbers for the country

options.name: --exclude-all-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --no-exclude-all-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require an Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --exclude-foreign-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --no-exclude-foreign-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a foreign Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --exclude-local-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --no-exclude-local-address-required
options.description: Whether to exclude phone numbers that require a local Address. Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `false`

options.name: --fax-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive faxes. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --no-fax-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive faxes. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --friendly-name
options.description: A descriptive string that you created to describe the new phone number. It can be up to 64 characters long. By default, this is a formatted version of the new phone number

options.name: --identity-sid
options.description: The SID of the Identity resource that we should associate with the new phone number. Some regions require an identity to meet local regulations

options.name: --in-lata
options.description: Limit results to a specific local access and transport area (LATA). Given a phone number, search within the same LATA as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --in-locality
options.description: Limit results to a particular locality or city. Given a phone number, search within the same Locality as that number

options.name: --in-postal-code
options.description: Limit results to a particular postal code. Given a phone number, search within the same postal code as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --in-rate-center
options.description: Limit results to a specific rate center, or given a phone number search within the same rate center as that number. Requires `in_lata` to be set as well. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --in-region
options.description: Limit results to a particular region, state, or province. Given a phone number, search within the same region as that number. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --limit
options.description: The maximum number of resources to return. Use '--no-limit' to disable

options.name: --mms-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive MMS messages. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --no-mms-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive MMS messages. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --near-lat-long
options.description: Given a latitude/longitude pair `lat,long` find geographically close numbers within `distance` miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --near-number
options.description: Given a phone number, find a geographically close number within `distance` miles. Distance defaults to 25 miles. Applies to only phone numbers in the US and Canada

options.name: --no-header
options.description: Skip including of headers while listing the data

options.name: --page-size
options.description: How many resources to return in each list page. The default is 50, and the maximum is 1000

options.name: --properties
options.description: The properties you would like to display (JSON output always shows all properties)

options.name: --sms-application-sid
options.description: The SID of the application that should handle SMS messages sent to the new phone number. If an `sms_application_sid` is present, we ignore all of the `sms_*_url` urls and use those set on the application

options.name: --sms-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive text messages. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --no-sms-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive text messages. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --sms-fallback-method
options.description: The HTTP method that we should use to call `sms_fallback_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`

options.name: --sms-fallback-url
options.description: The URL that we should call when an error occurs while requesting or executing the TwiML defined by `sms_url`

options.name: --sms-method
options.description: The HTTP method that we should use to call `sms_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`

options.name: --sms-url
options.description: The URL we should call when the new phone number receives an incoming SMS message

options.name: --status-callback
options.description: The URL we should call using the `status_callback_method` to send status information to your application

options.name: --status-callback-method
options.description: The HTTP method we should use to call `status_callback`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`

options.name: --trunk-sid
options.description: The SID of the Trunk we should use to handle calls to the new phone number. If a `trunk_sid` is present, we ignore all of the voice urls and voice applications and use only those set on the Trunk. Setting a `trunk_sid` will automatically delete your `voice_application_sid` and vice versa

options.name: --voice-application-sid
options.description: The SID of the application we should use to handle calls to the new phone number. If a `voice_application_sid` is present, we ignore all of the voice urls and use only those set on the application. Setting a `voice_application_sid` will automatically delete your `trunk_sid` and vice versa

options.name: --voice-caller-id-lookup
options.description: Whether to lookup the caller's name from the CNAM database and post it to your app. Can be: `true` or `false` and defaults to `false`

options.name: --no-voice-caller-id-lookup
options.description: Whether to lookup the caller's name from the CNAM database and post it to your app. Can be: `true` or `false` and defaults to `false`

options.name: --voice-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --no-voice-enabled
options.description: Whether the phone numbers can receive calls. Can be: `true` or `false`

options.name: --voice-fallback-method
options.description: The HTTP method that we should use to call `voice_fallback_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`

options.name: --voice-fallback-url
options.description: The URL that we should call when an error occurs retrieving or executing the TwiML requested by `url`

options.name: --voice-method
options.description: The HTTP method that we should use to call `voice_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`

options.name: --voice-receive-mode
options.description: The configuration parameter for the new phone number to receive incoming voice calls or faxes. Can be: `fax` or `voice` and defaults to `voice`

options.name: --voice-url
options.description: The URL that we should call to answer a call to the new phone number. The `voice_url` will not be called if a `voice_application_sid` or a `trunk_sid` is set

options.name: -agent-address
options.description: Address of the Agent. This can also be specified via the VAULT_AGENT_ADDR environment variable

options.name: -ca-cert
options.description: Path on the local disk to a single PEM-encoded CA certificate to verify the Vault server's SSL certificate. This takes precedence over -ca-path. This can also be specified via the VAULT_CACERT environment variable

options.name: -ca-path
options.description: Path on the local disk to a directory of PEM-encoded CA certificates to verify the Vault server's SSL certificate. This can also be specified via the VAULT_CAPATH environment variable

options.name: -client-cert
options.description: Path on the local disk to a single PEM-encoded CA certificate to use for TLS authentication to the Vault server. If this flag is specified, -client-key is also required. This can also be specified via the VAULT_CLIENT_CERT environment variable

options.name: -client-key
options.description: Path on the local disk to a single PEM-encoded private key matching the client certificate from -client-cert. This can also be specified via the VAULT_CLIENT_KEY environment variable

options.name: -header-key
options.description: Key-value pair provided as key=value to provide http header added to any request done by the CLI.Trying to add headers starting with 'X-Vault-' is forbidden and will make the command fail This can be specified multiple times

options.name: -mfa
options.description: Supply MFA credentials as part of X-Vault-MFA header. This can also be specified via the VAULT_MFA environment variable

options.name: -namespace
options.description: The namespace to use for the command. Setting this is not necessary but allows using relative paths. -ns can be used as shortcut. The default is (not set). This can also be specified via the VAULT_NAMESPACE environment variable

options.name: -non-interactive
options.description: When set true, prevents asking the user for input via the terminal. The default is false

options.name: -output-curl-string
options.description: Instead of executing the request, print an equivalent cURL command string and exit. The default is false

options.name: -policy-override

options.name: -tls-skip-verify

options.name: -unlock-key

options.description: Reset the rekeying progress. This will discard any submitted unseal keys or configuration. The default is false

options.name: -init
options.description: Initialize the rekeying operation. This can only be done if no rekeying operation is in progress. Customize the new number of key shares and key threshold using the -key-shares and -key-threshold flags. The default is false

options.name: -key-shares
options.description: Number of key shares to split the generated root key into. This is the number of 'unseal keys' to generate. This is aliased as '-n'. The default is 5

options.name: -key-threshold
options.description: Number of key shares required to reconstruct the root key. This must be less than or equal to -key-shares. This is aliased as '-t'. The default is 3

options.name: -nonce
options.description: Nonce value provided at initialization. The same nonce value must be provided with each unseal key

options.name: -pgp-keys
options.description: Comma-separated list of paths to files on disk containing public PGP keys OR a comma-separated list of Keybase usernames using the format 'keybase:<username>'. When supplied, the generated unseal keys will be encrypted and base64-encoded in the order specified in this list. The number of entries must match -key-shares, unless -stored-shares are used

options.name: -status
options.description: Print the status of the current attempt without providing an unseal key. The default is false

options.name: -target
options.description: Target for rekeying. 'recovery' only applies when HSM support is enabled. The default is barrier

options.name: -verify
options.description: Indicates that the action (-status, -cancel, or providing a key share) will be affecting verification for the current rekey attempt. The default is false

options.name: -backup
options.description: Store a backup of the current PGP encrypted unseal keys in Vault's core. The encrypted values can be recovered in the event of failure or discarded after success. See the -backup-delete and -backup-retrieve options for more information. This option only applies when the existing unseal keys were PGP encrypted. The default is false

options.name: -backup-delete
options.description: Delete any stored backup unseal keys. The default is false

options.name: -backup-retries
options.description: Retrieve the backed-up unseal keys. This option is only available if the PGP keys were provided and the backup has not been deleted. The default is false

options.description: Explicit maximum lifetime for the token. Unlike normal TTLs, the maximum TTL is a hard limit and cannot be exceeded. This is specified as a numeric string with suffix like '30s' or '5m'

options.description: Value for the token. By default, this is an auto-generated string. Specifying this value requires sudo permissions

options.name: -metadata

options.name: -no-default-policy
options.description: Detach the 'default' policy from the policy set for this token. The default is false

options.name: -orphan
options.description: Create the token with no parent. This prevents the token from being revoked when the token which created it expires. Setting this value requires root or sudo permissions. The default is false

options.name: -period
options.description: If specified, every renewal will use the given period. Periodic tokens do not expire (unless -explicit-max-ttl is also provided). Setting this value requires sudo permissions. This is specified as a numeric string with suffix like '30s' or '5m'

options.name: -policy
options.description: Name of a policy to associate with this token. This can be specified multiple times to attach multiple policies

options.name: -renewable
options.description: Allow the token to be renewed up to it's maximum TTL. The default is true

options.name: -role
options.description: Name of the role to create the token against. Specifying -role may override other arguments. The locally authenticated Vault token must have permission for 'auth/token/create/<role>'

options.name: -ttl
options.description: Initial TTL to associate with the token. Token renewals may be able to extend beyond this value, depending on the configured maximum TTLs. This is specified as a numeric string with suffix like '30s' or '5m'

options.name: -type
options.description: The type of token to create. Can be 'service' or 'batch'. The default is service

options.name: -use-limit
options.description: Number of times this token can be used. After the last use, the token is automatically revoked. By default, tokens can be used an unlimited number of times until their expiration

subcommands.description: Create a POT file for a WordPress project

options.name: --slug
options.description: Plugin or theme slug. Defaults to the source directory’s basename

options.name: --domain
options.description: Text domain to look for in the source code, unless the --ignore-domain option is used. By default, the “Text Domain” header of the plugin or theme is used. If none is provided, it falls back to the project slug

options.name: --ignore-domain
options.description: Ignore the text domain completely and extract strings with any text domain

options.name: --merge
options.description: Comma-separated list of POT files whose contents should be merged with the extracted strings. If left empty, defaults to the destination POT file. POT file headers will be ignored

options.name: --subtract
options.description: Comma-separated list of POT files whose contents should act as some sort of blacklist for string extraction. Any string which is found on that blacklist will not be extracted. This can be useful when you want to create multiple POT files from the same source directory with slightly different content and no duplicate strings between them

options.name: --include
options.description: Comma-separated list of files and paths that should be used for string extraction. If provided, only these files and folders will be taken into account for string extraction. For example, --include='src,my-file.php will ignore anything besides my-file.php and files in the src directory. Simple glob patterns can be used, i.e. --include=foo-*.php includes any PHP file with the foo- prefix. Leading and trailing slashes are ignored, i.e. /my/directory/ is the same as my/directory

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Comma-separated list of files and paths that should be skipped for string extraction. For example, --exclude='.github,myfile.php would ignore any strings found within myfile.php or the .github folder. Simple glob patterns can be used, i.e. --exclude=foo-*.php excludes any PHP file with the foo- prefix. Leading and trailing slashes are ignored, i.e. /my/directory/ is the same as my/directory. The following files and folders are always excluded: node_modules, .git, .svn, .CVS, .hg, vendor, *.min.js

options.name: --headers
options.description: Array in JSON format of custom headers which will be added to the POT file. Defaults to empty array

options.name: --skip-js
options.description: Skips JavaScript string extraction. Useful when this is done in another build step, e.g. through Babel

options.name: --skip-php
options.description: Skips PHP string extraction

options.name: --skip-block-json
options.description: Skips string extraction from block.json files

options.name: --skip-audit
options.description: Skips string audit where it tries to find possible mistakes in translatable strings. Useful when running in an automated environment

options.name: --file-comment
options.description: String that should be added as a comment to the top of the resulting POT file. By default, a copyright comment is added for WordPress plugins and themes in the following manner: Copyright (C) 2018 Example Plugin Author. This file is distributed under the same license as the Example Plugin package. If a plugin or theme specifies a license in their main plugin file or stylesheet, the comment looks like this: Copyright (C) 2018 Example Plugin Author. This file is distributed under the GPLv2

options.name: --package-name
options.description: Name to use for package name in the resulting POT file’s Project-Id-Version header. Overrides plugin or theme name, if applicable

args.description: Directory to scan for string extraction

args.name: destination
args.description: Name of the resulting POT file

options.name: -fstack-protector
options.description: Enable stack protectors for some functions vulnerable to stack smashing. This uses a loose heuristic which considers functions vulnerable if they contain a char (or 8bit integer) array or constant sized calls to alloca , which are of greater size than ssp-buffer-size (default: 8 bytes). All variable sized calls to alloca are considered vulnerable. A function with a stack protector has a guard value added to the stack frame that is checked on function exit. The guard value must be positioned in the stack frame such that a buffer overflow from a vulnerable variable will overwrite the guard value before overwriting the function's return address. The reference stack guard value is stored in a global variable
